created_by: Dylan L.R. Pollock with Atlas continuity support
description: Master Plan v122.0 formalizes the physical assembly, surface color finish, storage architecture, and compute baseline for the Monkey-Head-Project. It details the Huey V4 shell assembly merging the V3 physical base with V2 donor parts, establishing a metallic silver primary finish with deep rich purple accents across spray-painted plastic and sanded/primed wood surfaces. It specifies primary project storage as two 10 TB hard drives in a RAID 1 redundant array alongside lab stocks of 16 GB M.2 SSDs. It locks the Huey Brain core workstation hardware to an ASUS TUF Gaming Z790-Plus WiFi motherboard paired with an Intel Core i9-12900K processor, and explicitly confirms that the Lenovo Legion Go remains strictly dedicated LabTech, excluded from core Huey runtime execution.

explicit_decisions: The project is organized around Huey Brain, Huey Body, and Huey Farm.
Huey V4 physical shell assembly merges the V3 physical base with V2 donor material.

V4 physical finish scheme: metallic silver primary color with deep rich purple offset accents applied via spray paint to plastic and sanded/primed wood surfaces; metal structural components remain in original black or native finish unless otherwise specified.

Primary project storage consists of two 10 TB hard drives configured in a RAID 1 array for data redundancy; 16 GB M.2 SSDs are available from lab stock for modular boot/swap needs; 2.5-inch SSDs remain unassigned reserve stock.
Huey Brain core workstation hardware is confirmed as an ASUS TUF Gaming Z790-Plus WiFi motherboard paired with an Intel 12th-Gen Core i9-12900K processor.
Lenovo Legion Go is explicitly classified as dedicated LabTech / support hardware, completely excluded from Huey Brain, Body, and Farm core runtime execution.
PyHuey GUI is the primary interface and a core runtime component intended for extensive use under Python 3.13.
The target canonical Python namespace is hueyos; useful huey and legacy material is to be rewritten and merged deliberately.
Three Nvidia Tesla V100 32 GB GPUs will be pooled to provide 96 GB of VRAM for large-model hosting, transcription, and agentic workflows.
A separate basic discrete GPU provides display output and system boot graphics.
Power delivery relies on two linked, high-capacity PSUs for load distribution.
Liquid cooling loop utilizes car-grade coolant, a sealed bucket within a garbage bin secondary containment vessel, and a battery backup dedicated to pump and fan operation[cite: 1, 4].
Only Dylan L.R. Pollock may lock project canon[cite: 1, 4].
